s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with fever and focal neurological deficits
salient_findings: High-grade fever for 14 days
Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Upper motor neuron type right-sided seventh cranial-nerve palsy
Complete hemiplegia
Multifocal discrete and confluent hypodensities on brain CT
key_facts: Progressive weakness on the right side of body for 5 days
Upper motor neuron type right-sided seventh cranial-nerve palsy
Extensor plantar response on the right
SARS-CoV-2 RNA detected on nasopharyngeal swab by RT-PCR
CSF examination showed pleocytosis with slightly increased protein

differentials: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
Mitochondrial Encephalomyopathy, Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke-like Episodes
per_call: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
Mitochondrial Encephalomyopathy, Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke-like Episodes

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the acute neurological syndrome with fever and focal neurological deficits, and is consistent with the CSF examination showing pleocytosis with slightly increased protein

shortlist.label: Cerebral Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Explains the multifocal smooth stenosis of intracranial arteries and the presence of fever and focal neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Rasmussen Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the progressive weakness on one side of the body, seizures, and the presence of fever

shortlist.label: Herpes Simplex Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: A possible cause of acute neurological syndrome with fever, and the presence of focal neurological deficits and CSF pleocytosis

shortlist.label: Acute Hemorrhagic Leukoencephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the acute onset of neurological symptoms, fever, and the presence of multifocal discrete and confluent hypodensities on the brain CT

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including high-grade fever, throbbing headache, vomiting, progressive weakness on one side of the body, and the presence of pleocytosis with slightly increased protein in the CSF, along with multifocal discrete and confluent hypodensities in the brain CT, are consistent with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM), especially given the recent SARS-CoV-2 infection which can trigger ADEM.

rejected.label: Cerebral Vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has multifocal smooth stenosis of intracranial arteries, the overall clinical and imaging findings are more suggestive of an inflammatory process like ADEM rather than a primary vasculitis.

rejected.label: Rasmussen Encephalitis
rejected.why: Rasmussen Encephalitis typically presents with more chronic and progressive symptoms, often with a history of seizures, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Herpes Simplex Encephalitis
rejected.why: The CSF examination did not specifically indicate the presence of herpes simplex virus, and the imaging findings, although suggestive of encephalitis, do not specifically point towards herpes simplex encephalitis.

rejected.label: Acute Hemorrhagic Leukoencephalitis
rejected.why: The patient's imaging studies do not show the characteristic hemorrhagic components that are typical of Acute Hemorrhagic Leukoencephalitis.
